currentUse: Community center — the All Saints Neighborhood Center, home base of the nonprofit Urban Neighborhood Initiatives (UNI) at 8300 Longworth St. in Detroit's Springwells neighborhood
summary: Šv. Petro (St. Peter) was founded in 1920 as a distinct Lithuanian parish for Detroit's growing Delray community; its church opened in 1921. The modest church still stands in southwest Detroit and has been converted to secular community use. The Archdiocese of Detroit's closed-parishes register gives 1921–1995, using the church-opening year rather than the parish's 1920 institutional founding. After the 1995 closure, the church's statues, furniture, and the large Lithuanian wayside cross that stood in front of the building were donated to Lithuania; the brick cladding added in the parish's late Lithuanian era was removed and the original wooden exterior restored (Global True Lithuania). Beginning in 1997, All Saints Catholic Parish and the nonprofit now called Urban Neighborhood Initiatives (founded 1997 as Neighborhood Centers Incorporated) restored the empty church building into the All Saints Neighborhood Center, a hub for youth and adult programs in the Springwells neighborhood. The center holds some historical plaques about the building's Lithuanian past in the first room beyond the entrance, but the building otherwise retains no Lithuanian details. UNI remains active at 8300 Longworth St., Detroit, MI 48209 as of 2026, with annual reports published through 2025.

historicalNarrative.text: Lithuanian families drawn to Detroit's automobile industry established a growing community in Delray before the First World War. They initially traveled across the city to Šv. Jurgio for Lithuanian worship. In 1920, a separate Lithuanian parish was founded for Delray under Father Jurgis Jonaitis; its first services were held at nearby Holy Cross Hungarian Catholic Church.

historicalNarrative.text: The community acquired land at Mullane and Longworth and raised its own church in 1921. The church and the parish therefore have different start dates: Šv. Petro's institutional life begins in 1920, while its church-building history begins in 1921. The parish remained there until its closure in 1995.

developments.detail: Lithuanians in southwest Detroit had previously traveled to Šv. Jurgio for worship. St. Peter parish was founded in 1920 under Father Jurgis Jonaitis and first celebrated Mass at nearby Holy Cross Hungarian Catholic Church.

developments.headline: The parish opened its church at Mullane and Longworth
developments.detail: After worshipping temporarily at Holy Cross, the St. Peter community raised its own small church in 1921 at Mullane and Longworth. This is the building that survived the parish's 1995 closure and later became the All Saints Neighborhood Center.

developments.headline: Parish closed; contents sent to Lithuania
developments.detail: The Archdiocese of Detroit's closed-parishes list records St. Peter Lithuanian Parish (Detroit) as 1921–1995, with no note on where sacramental records went. Per Global True Lithuania, the church's statues and furniture were donated to Lithuania, as was the large Lithuanian-style wayside cross that stood in front of the church.

developments.headline: Empty church restored as All Saints Neighborhood Center
developments.detail: Urban Neighborhood Initiatives (founded 1997 as Neighborhood Centers Incorporated by All Saints Catholic Parish parishioners) began with the restoration of the empty church building into the All Saints Neighborhood Center, a community hub in the Springwells neighborhood of southwest Detroit. Global True Lithuania confirms the community center has operated in the former St. Peter building since 1997, put up historical plaques in the entrance room, and that the wooden facade (brick-covered in the late Lithuanian era) was restored to its original appearance.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: No contradictions. The archive record is corroborated on every point: diocesan closure in 1995 (AOD lists the parish as 1921–1995), closure tied to the retirement of the last pastor (search excerpts of Detroit1701.org name him as Fr. Casimir Burkus — plausible refinement of the archive's unnamed 'pastor retired'), and contents shipped to Lithuania (Global True Lithuania specifies statues, furniture, and the front-yard wayside cross were donated to Lithuania). Refinements: founding can now be dated — parish founded 1920, church built/opened 1921 (AOD gives 1921–1995 as parish dates; Detroit1701 excerpts say founded 1920 with the building raised by 1921). The parish is confirmed distinct from Detroit Šv. Antano (AOD lists St. Anthony Lithuanian separately, 1920–2013) and Southfield Dievo Apvaizdos (Divine Providence, still listed as records repository).
gaps: No property-transaction record, sale price, or current deed holder was found; whether the archdiocese, All Saints Parish, or UNI owns the building today remains unverified. No recent preservation campaign or Lithuanian community activity at the building was identified. Parish-history pages and a 1960 church photograph supplied on 2026-08-01 corroborate the 1920 founding and 1921 church-opening distinction and give a July 10, 1921 dedication date, but the scanned volume's exact title, publisher, and stable archive URL still need to be identified before that page-level citation is published.
